chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'adah ibn Sadah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade seeking cure in the hammat (hot springs), which are the hot springs that are in the mountains from which the smell of sulfur is found, for indeed they emerge from the exhalation of Hell.
ai.seo_question: Why are hot springs with a sulfur smell prohibited for seeking cure in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration linking the physical property of sulfur in hot springs to their eschatological origin as exhalations from Hell. This establishes a theological basis for the prohibition of *istishfa'* (seeking cure) in these specific springs, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that their impurity is not merely physical but spiritual, derived from their connection to *Jahannam*. The ruling underscores the integration of natural phenomena with divine signs in traditional Islamic medicine and jurisprudence.
